first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this, so I read it properly. The opening about a family visiting another family to ask the question is lovely and calm, nothing trendy about it. I could tell straight away it was going to be about holding the wedding somewhere other than Lebanon, which is a relief, because that was my first worry.

journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Lebanon "Do not travel" (as at November 2026), so this guide is about bringing the customs to a wedding elsewhere.
journey.reaction: Good. They've checked the government advice and told me plainly. That's the sort of thing I'd want a planner to know without me having to raise it.

journey.quote: The practical point for planning: ask both families early which steps they want, rather than working from a list.
journey.reaction: Sensible. Two families paying and both with opinions, so yes, that conversation has to happen first. I'll pass that line to my husband.

journey.section: The church ceremony and the crowning
journey.quote: The Orthodox Church in America text follows the same shape: a Service of Betrothal at the back of the church, with the rings blessed and exchanged, and then the Service of Crowning in the centre.
journey.reaction: This part reads a bit like a reference book, one source after another. I followed it, but on the iPad it felt heavy. I don't need to know which website said what, I need to know what happens and what to arrange.

journey.section: Space for the zaffeh and the dabke line
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms these with the venue in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: That's what I want to hear. Someone checks the noise rules in writing, before we've paid anything. I'd rather that than find out on the night the drums have to stop at ten.

journey.section: Timing a henna night around travel
journey.quote: A henna night works best once the close family has landed and slept.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Finally someone thinking about the older ones getting off a long flight. But it stops there. My mother and my husband's aunt will be coming, and nothing in this tells me about getting them up stairs, onto a terrace or from the airport.

journey.section: Blades, venue rules and the cake
journey.quote: If a family heirloom is travelling with you, check your airline's rules and the destination's rules on carrying a blade well ahead of the flight.
journey.reaction: Practical, and exactly what my brother-in-law would forget to check. Good catch.

journey.section: Blades, venue rules and the cake
journey.quote: Your Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel and vendors, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms what is included in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This is the sentence that matters to me. One person, fee in writing first. It doesn't say anything about deposits or what happens if a supplier lets us down, but it's a good start.

journey.section: A note on travel and marriage law
journey.quote: You can't register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is recognised if it was valid where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that and I'm glad it's here. It's the kind of question I'd feel silly asking, and they've answered it without making me feel old-fashioned.

unanswered_questions: My mother uses a walking frame. Will someone check the venue's steps, terraces and transfers for elderly guests?
Is the deposit protected if an overseas supplier or venue lets us down?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Italian time?
Are quotes and contracts in Australian dollars and in English, or will we be signing Italian contracts in euros?
Do you advise on travel insurance for older guests travelling for the wedding?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked?

turn_offs_found.quote: The Melkite Greek Catholic Eparchy of Newton calls the Eastern Churches' marriage service the Mystery of Crowning.
turn_offs_found.why: The ceremony section stacks one named source after another. It's not wrong, it just reads like homework rather than advice from a person, and it's the one stretch where my eyes started to glaze.

would_share_with: My husband, with the Advisor paragraph and the marriage law note marked
My sister, for the henna night and sweets sections

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like one person to hold all of this together, you can speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: The fee in writing and the single contact are what I'm after. I'd click if I knew it led to a phone call with a named person, not a form that goes into a void. I'd rather my daughter make the first contact, then I'd want to talk to them myself.

top_3_changes: Add one or two practical lines on older guests: venue access, steps, transfers and rest days, alongside the henna night timing advice.
In the Advisor paragraph, say in a few words what happens after you click (for example a phone call) and who is responsible if a supplier falls through, if the business can confirm it.
Lighten the crowning section: keep what happens and what to arrange, and move some of the source-by-source attributions out of the reading flow.
